relevance_note: Case report of a man and his son 'both heterozygous for a pathogenic missense E250K mutation in the PSTPIP1 gene', plus a literature table (Table I) of previously reported E250K patients with individual-level detail.
method_note: Read the paper manually; a short Python script in the scratch directory assembled the JSON from hand-entered values and the five Table I rows (checked against the table). Labels: index case = 'patient' (single first-hand case; role words only); his son = 'son of patient' (paper says 'his infant son'); Table I has no label column, so rows are 'Table I row 1'-'Table I row 5', with the Author (y) cell as source_reference_in_review; the previously reported E250K patient with FSGS cited to reference 10 (mentioned only in the Discussion, but with variant and feature) = 'ref ^10 patient'. Table I 'Age (y)' is unspecified; recorded as age at last evaluation/report (uncertain whether it is age at report or at onset). Table I title prints the gene as 'PTSPIP1' (typo); table notes and text print 'PSTPIP1', which was recorded with both spans. Variant for Table I and ref 10 patients is from the table title / sentence (E250K); no zygosity, inheritance or pathogenicity is given for them. Protein change printed as 'E250K' (no 'p.' prefix) and cDNA as 'c.748 glycine to adenine' (non-HGVS wording); both kept as printed. Contradiction/inconsistency: text says '6 previously reported patients with the E250K mutation' and calls this 'the seventh published case', but Table I lists only 5 previously reported patients; the ref 10 patient (Borgia 2021) is not in Table I and may or may not be the sixth. Sentence 'Additional features present in other cases with the E250K mutation include splenomegaly, bleeding diathesis, and serious cutaneous and pulmonary infections.^6' cites ref 6 for 'other cases' (plural); attribution to the Table I Lindwall row is ambiguous, so these features were not recorded for any person. Lindwall row 'osteomyelitis' recorded as observed for the checklist item 'sterile osteomyelitis or osteolytic bone lesions' though the table does not say sterile. 'hepatosplenomegaly' in Table I recorded as observed splenomegaly and hepatomegaly. For the index patient, 'absence of ... hepatosplenomegaly, pancytopenia, and growth failure' was recorded as excluded features; it was not used to exclude splenomegaly, hepatomegaly, anemia, neutropenia or thrombocytopenia separately (narrow vs broad rule), but excluded the growth failure checklist item. The index patient's renal disease is attributed by the authors to multiple other factors as well (nephrolithiasis, hypertension, sepsis, cyclosporine); recorded as observed kidney involvement as stated. Son: inheritance recorded as 'inherited paternal' because the paper states the father carries the same variant; no son features are reported beyond 'a possible autoinflammatory syndrome', so his checklist is all not reported. Group-level literature counts (16 of 63, 18 of 21) describe no individuals and were not extracted. n_patients_reported and cites_prior_report left null (no number or statement given).
